Sample metadata and `patch.diff` instead point at later commit pair `0e8bdfce66ba4b2fef79a2525fd83ecfc22b0983` / `c473b21cff5e1a459b4467f18bf7414114f848fd`; the saved patch corroborates related frame/chunk hardening work, but the live staged checkout reproduces a different still-vulnerable path that trusts a forged in-memory `chunk_cbytes`.

classification.classification_note: The saved ASan report is a 117791-byte read at the right edge of the 27249-byte fuzz-input region. The immediate faulty state is an unchecked in-memory `chunk_cbytes` from `frame_get_lazychunk()`, which makes later dictionary-size checks compare against a forged `srcsize` instead of the actual remaining frame bytes.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42491502 (c-blosc2): Heap-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target decompress_frame_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42491502
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / exact staged vulnerable source from gt-arvo_42491502-workspace:/src/c-blosc2 / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged poc bytes
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run reproduces the crash against the staged ARVO checkout `474ebf151be847186e6bc2c1381a8f7d4beff4dd`, whose line map matches `ZSTD_initDDict_internal:134`, `initialize_context_decompression:1648`, and `frame_decompress_chunk:1675`. The exact 27249-byte witness is admitted by `blosc2_frame_from_sframe()` because bytes 16-23 encode `frame_len = 27249`, so the frame aliases `frame->sdata` directly to the attacker buffer. `get_header_info()` reparses bytes 11-14 as `header_len = 92`, bytes 30-37 as `nbytes = 18747392`, bytes 39-46 as `cbytes = 26857`, and bytes 53-56 as `chunksize = 256000`, so `schunk->nchunks` becomes `74` and the harness enters the frame-backed decompression loop. `get_coffsets()` points at byte 26949, where the witness stores a `memcpyed` extended-header offsets chunk whose raw 64-bit payload begins with offsets `[0, 40, 2351, 4700, 7877, 10236, 13593, 16812, 20616, 22995]`; the first offset entry consistent with the saved `ZSTD_createDDict` stack is `40`, so `frame_get_lazychunk()` points `src` at byte 132. That pointed header claims `nbytes = 256000`, `blocksize = 256000`, `cbytes = 738199815`, sets `BLOSC2_USEDICT` in byte 31, and stores `dict_size = 117791` at `src + 36`. Vulnerable `frame_get_lazychunk()` returns the forged `chunk_cbytes` without checking that the chunk fits inside the remaining `27117` bytes of the frame, so `blosc2_decompress_ctx()` is called with attacker-chosen `srcsize = 738199815`. `initialize_context_decompression()` therefore accepts the header (`sourcesize == destsize`, `cbytes == srcsize`), computes `nblocks = 1`, enters the dictionary path, and sets `dict_buffer = src + 40` (overall byte 172). Only `27077` bytes remain from that pointer to the end of the input, but `ZSTD_createDDict()` copies `117791` bytes, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read. The saved `patch.diff` is from later zero-runlen/header-overhead work and does not add the missing in-memory frame-bounds check on `chunk_cbytes`, so it does not directly patch this live reproduced path.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that parses vulnerability-relevant frame metadata from the attacker buffer.
source.value_from: The staged 27249-byte `poc` stores `00 00 00 00 00 00 6a 71` at bytes 16-23, so this statement materializes `frame_len = 27249`, matching the full input size and keeping the buffer on the in-memory frame path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After `get_coffset()` selects byte 132 of the attacker buffer as a chunk header, the in-memory lazy-chunk path trusts that header's `cbytes` field and returns it as `srcsize` without proving the claimed chunk fits inside the frame.
root_cause.note: The missing obligation on the witnessed path is a frame-bounds check such as `header_len + offset + chunk_cbytes <= frame->len` before returning the chunk to `blosc2_decompress_ctx()`. On the witness, only `27249 - 132 = 27117` bytes remain from the claimed chunk start, but this line materializes `chunk_cbytes = 738199815`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. Vendored Zstd copies `117791` bytes from the attacker-selected dictionary pointer, which starts 172 bytes into the 27249-byte fuzz input and runs past the right boundary of the buffer.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 117791` at this line with stack `ZSTD_initDDict_internal -> ZSTD_createDDict_advanced -> ZSTD_createDDict -> initialize_context_decompression -> frame_decompress_chunk`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This decodes attacker-controlled 64-bit chunk offsets from the frame's in-memory offsets chunk. The raw payload begins with offsets `0` and `40`; the first entry consistent with the saved `ZSTD_createDDict` stack is `offset = 40`, which directs `frame_get_lazychunk()` to byte 132 of the fuzz buffer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: At byte 26949 the witness stores a `memcpyed` extended-header offsets chunk (`flags = 0x07`, `typesize = 8`, `nbytes = 80`, `blocksize = 80`, `cbytes = 112`). Its 80-byte raw payload encodes the ten 64-bit offsets `[0, 40, 2351, 4700, 7877, 10236, 13593, 16812, 20616, 22995]`.

parser_admitted.description: The open-sframe path passes `copy = false`, so even though `nchunks` is positive the parser keeps the object frame-backed. Later chunk requests therefore go through `frame_get_lazychunk()` on the attacker buffer instead of copying validated chunks out of the frame.

evidence_limitations: The exact staged vulnerable source that reproduced the crash is the ARVO workspace checkout `474ebf151be847186e6bc2c1381a8f7d4beff4dd`, not metadata vulnerable commit `0e8bdfce66ba4b2fef79a2525fd83ecfc22b0983`; every line number below is anchored to the staged checkout because it matches the saved ASan stack.

The saved `patch.diff` and fixed commit `c473b21cff5e1a459b4467f18bf7414114f848fd` are from later zero-runlen/header-overhead work and do not add a bound on in-memory `lazychunk_cbytes`, so Stage 02 cannot use that diff as direct fix evidence for this reproduced path.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not instrument. The saved run does not print the exact `nchunk` value, so the crash is closed by decoding the witness offsets payload and identifying `offset = 40` as the first chunk header consistent with the reproduced `ZSTD_createDDict` stack.

fine_trace.note: Source. The in-memory frame parser reads the serialized frame length directly from attacker bytes 16-23. In the staged witness those bytes decode to `frame_len = 27249`.
The size sanity check is the first parser admission gate. Because the fuzz input length is also 27249, the function does not return `NULL` and continues materializing the frame.
Because `copy` is false, the frame keeps a direct alias to the attacker buffer. Every later metadata read on this path dereferences `frame->sdata` rather than a validated copy.
Reparsing attacker bytes 11-14 yields `header_len = 92`. This is the base offset later added to both the compressed-data size and the decoded chunk offset.
Reparsing attacker bytes 39-46 yields `cbytes = 26857`. In the in-memory frame path this places the compressed-offsets chunk at `frame->sdata + 92 + 26857`, i.e. byte 26949.

The same header reparse sees positive `FRAME_NBYTES = 18747392` and `FRAME_CHUNKSIZE = 256000`, so this branch computes `nchunks = 74`. That positive count keeps the frame-backed decompression loop reachable beyond chunk 0.

With step 4 `header_len = 92` and step 5 `cbytes = 26857`, the in-memory path returns `frame->sdata + 26949`. At that byte the witness stores a `memcpyed` extended-header offsets chunk whose raw 80-byte payload contains ten 64-bit offsets.

The offsets chunk payload begins with the 64-bit values `[0, 40, 2351, 4700, 7877, 10236, 13593, 16812, 20616, 22995]`. The first payload entry (`0`) points at a header whose `blosc2_flags` byte is zero, so the earliest entry consistent with the saved `ZSTD_createDDict` stack is the second one, materializing `offset = 40` on the crashing iteration.
The selected chunk base becomes `frame->sdata + 92 + 40`, i.e. byte 132 of the attacker buffer. The bytes there begin `04 01 35 04 00 e8 03 00 00 e8 03 00 07 09 00 2c`.

Root cause. Bytes 144-147 of the witness are `07 09 00 2c`, so `sw32_()` materializes `chunk_cbytes = 738199815`. The function returns that forged size even though only `27249 - 132 = 27117` bytes remain from the claimed chunk start.

The pointed header claims `nbytes_ = 256000`, and the caller-supplied destination capacity for each frame chunk is also `256000`, so this guard does not stop the path before the oversized `srcsize` is passed into the decompressor.

The chunk header at byte 132 materializes `header_flags = 0x35`, `typesize = 4`, `sourcesize = 256000`, `blocksize = 256000`, and `cbytes = 738199815`. These present guards all pass because step 10 supplied the same forged `srcsize = 738199815` and step 11 already proved `destsize = 256000`.
From step 12's `sourcesize = blocksize = 256000`, the decompressor derives `nblocks = 1`. That single-block count determines where the code expects the dictionary-size field to live.

Because step 12's `header_flags = 0x35` has both shuffle bits set, the extended-header branch runs. Byte 163 of the witness is `0x1f`, so `BLOSC2_USEDICT` is set and the dictionary-handling path becomes reachable.
With step 13 `nblocks = 1` and step 14 `bstarts_offset = 32`, the code chooses `bstarts_end = 36`. The would-be dictionary size is therefore read from `src + 36`.
Bytes 168-171 of the pointed header are `1f cc 01 00`, so this statement materializes `dict_size = 117791`. That is exactly the read size reported by ASan at the later `memcpy()` sink.

The present size check still passes because step 10 supplied forged `srcsize = 738199815`, which is much larger than step 16's `dict_size = 117791`. The dictionary pointer becomes `src + 40`, i.e. overall byte 172 of the input, where only `27249 - 172 = 27077` bytes remain.

Sink. The call uses step 17's `dict_buffer` and step 16's `dict_size = 117791`. Because only 27077 bytes remain from byte 172 to the end of the 27249-byte input, this copy reads 90714 bytes past the right edge of the attacker buffer and matches the saved ASan report.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, and the staged `patch.diff` does not add a bound on in-memory `lazychunk_cbytes` or on the later dictionary copy path from `frame_get_lazychunk()`, so it cannot be used as direct resolution proof for this staged crash.

poc.trigger: Pass the exact staged 27249-byte `poc` to `decompress_frame_fuzzer`; its frame header creates a frame-backed `schunk` with `nchunks = 74`, its in-frame offsets chunk materializes the crashing `offset = 40`, and the pointed header at byte 132 makes Zstd copy a 117791-byte dictionary from byte 172 of the input.

format.name: serialized blosc2 in-memory frame
format.contract: Exactly the staged 27249-byte buffer in `poc` (sha256 `8e99e9e303518b4d8826355e63e8c43b3cd24ceda038d08f3e6f1279c16e69f8`). Its verified trigger semantics are limited to the concrete field values this witness sets: frame bytes 11-14 are `00 00 00 5c` (`header_len = 92`), bytes 16-23 are `00 00 00 00 00 00 6a 71` (`frame_len = 27249`), bytes 30-37 are `00 00 00 00 01 1e 10 00` (`nbytes = 18747392`), bytes 39-46 are `00 00 00 00 00 00 68 e9` (`cbytes = 26857`), and bytes 53-56 are `00 03 e8 00` (`chunksize = 256000`). At byte 26949 the in-frame offsets chunk begins with header bytes `04 01 07 08 50 00 00 00 50 00 00 00 70 00 00 00`; because it is a `memcpyed` extended-header chunk, its 80-byte raw payload encodes the 64-bit offsets `[0, 40, 2351, 4700, 7877, 10236, 13593, 16812, 20616, 22995]`. The header pointed to by offset 40 starts at byte 132 and begins `04 01 35 04 00 e8 03 00 00 e8 03 00 07 09 00 2c`; byte 163 is `1f` (`BLOSC2_USEDICT` set), bytes 168-171 are `1f cc 01 00` (`dict_size = 117791`), and the dictionary bytes start at byte 172. Those exact values make the in-memory frame path return `chunk_cbytes = 738199815`, make `initialize_context_decompression()` accept the forged bounds, and make `ZSTD_initDDict_internal()` copy 117791 bytes from a region with only 27077 bytes remaining. Stage 01 only proves this exact blob and observed path; it does not generalize to other frames, other offset tables, or nearby dictionary sizes.
